clips.start_words: Your son made a documentary about you
clips.send: A friend sends this to someone who always blames others - it names the real cause, with awe.
clips.caption:
A journalist once handed Deepak Chopra his own son's documentary - a film that tore him apart on camera.

Chopra's answer silenced the room: "My son didn't make a documentary about me. He made a documentary about himself."

Kevin Trudeau says that line holds a law most people never apply. Life is a mirror, and the people who infuriate you most are reflecting something back at you - not revealing something about them.

Think about the last person who made your blood boil today. What does that reaction actually say about you?

clips.start_words: When I was young and free
clips.send: A parent sends this to a grown child still trying to fix everyone else - the regret of a dying man, pure anxiety.
clips.caption:
In 1100 AD, someone carved a confession into a bishop's tomb inside Westminster Abbey.

He wrote that as a young man he dreamed of changing the world. Older, he settled for changing his country. Older still, just his own family - and they wouldn't listen either.

On his deathbed he admitted the truth: if he had only changed himself first, his example might have changed his family, then his country, then the world.

Kevin Trudeau says most of us are still trying to fix everyone except ourselves. Who are you still trying to change instead of starting with you?
